title: ICT Technician (ICTTech)
source: ICTTech Standard third edition, pp.18–23 (competence tables), transcribed verbatim from "icttech-3rd-edition conv.xls"
note: Text verified verbatim against "icttech-3rd-edition.pdf" pp.18–23. Five conversion artifacts in the xls ("dificulty", "eficiently" ×2, "ICTTechnician", missing spaces in "2.Accept"/"3.Accept") were corrected to match the PDF. "manufacturers requirements" (no apostrophe) is as printed in the PDF. Hard line-wraps have been unwrapped; the "E ... (continued)" heading on p.23 is merged into the single E table. No other words or punctuation changed.
columns: The applicant shall demonstrate that they:

groups.title: Knowledge and understanding
groups.framing: ICT Technicians shall use ICT knowledge and understanding to apply technical, practical and systems skills.
groups.explanation: This competence is about having knowledge of the technologies, standards and practices relevant to the applicant’s area of work and having evidence of maintaining and applying this knowledge.
groups.statementsIntro: The applicant shall demonstrate that they:

statements.text: Apply ICT principles in an analytical and systematic approach, to solve and review problems and contribute to continuous improvement
illustrativeExamples: Evaluating potential methods of carrying out an engineering task and selecting the most appropriate solution
Recognising a difficulty and then identifying an approach to resolve it
Identifying an improvement in a technique, procedure, process or method
Interpreting and carrying out test procedures

statements.text: Review, select and use appropriate techniques, procedures and methods to undertake activities.
illustrativeExamples: Drawing on your technical knowledge to complete a task
Performing calculations using standard formulae
Analysing performance or test data or comparing performance information with published material
Applying knowledge of modelling packages and an ability to use them to solve problems

groups.title: Design, development and solving ICT problems
groups.framing: ICT Technicians shall contribute to the design, development, configuration, testing, commissioning, installation, deployment, operation, migration or maintenance of ICT solutions, products, processes, systems, services or applications.
groups.explanation: This competence is about the ability to apply ICT knowledge effectively and efficiently to the individual tasks which need to be undertaken in the applicant’s role.
groups.statementsIntro: The applicant shall demonstrate that they:

statements.text: Identify and/or respond to problems with ICT solutions, services or infrastructure and apply suitable methods to seek the causes and to achieve the development of satisfactory solutions
illustrativeExamples: Using knowledge to identify a problem or an opportunity for improvement
Investigating a problem to identify the underlying cause
Identifying a solution to a problem or an improvement opportunity
Contributing to the design of an item or process

statements.text:
Identify, organise and use resources effectively to complete ICT tasks, with consideration for factors such as cost, performance, confidentiality, security, quality and availability of service, health, safety and environmental impact.
or
Configure or maintain ICT systems to provide satisfactory performance and quality of service.
or
Secure and protect ICT systems from intrusion, damage, attack or data loss.
illustrativeExamples: Balancing these factors in selecting appropriate materials
Identifying precautions as a result of evaluating risks and other factors
Considering how waste can be minimised, recycled or disposed of safely if recycling is not possible
Contributing to best practice methods of continuous improvement
Improving the quality of an operation or process
Ability to tailor and run simulation and other models
Ability to solve software and/or related technical problems under general guidance from more senior staff
Knowledge of LAN/WAN: installing equipment and software, upgrading, configuration, testing
System administration tasks in line with manufacturers requirements

groups.title: Responsibility, management and leadership
groups.framing: ICT Technicians shall accept and exercise personal responsibility.
groups.explanation: This competence is about the ability to plan and manage the applicant’s own work effectively and efficiently. It is also about the ability to consider and identify improvements to maintain quality in their work.
groups.statementsIntro: The applicant shall demonstrate that they:

statements.text: Work reliably and effectively on ICT tasks without close supervision and by adhering to the job instructions or best practice
illustrativeExamples: Completing challenging tasks successfully within your area of work
Identifying issues which fall outside of your current knowledge and seeking advice
Identifying standards and codes of practice relevant to a new task

statements.text: Accept responsibility for the work of themselves or others
illustrativeExamples: Fully understanding drawings, permits to work, instructions or other similar documents after appropriate checking, and identifying issues
Inspecting work carried out by others
Checking the status of equipment, the work environment and facilities and taking appropriate actions before commencing work

statements.text: Accept, allocate or supervise technical and other tasks
illustrativeExamples: Ensuring that the scope of a task is clear before accepting and/or allocating it to others
Querying any aspect of a task which is not clear and/or providing an explanation if a query is raised by others
Learning from your own experience and/or providing constructive feedback when supervising or working with others

statements.text: Be aware of and/or involved in continuous quality improvement.
illustrativeExamples: Demonstrate how you have contributed to relevant quality audits and where you have delivered against a quality improvement action
Examples of where you have reported a problem which has subsequently improved a process

groups.title: Communication and interpersonal skills
groups.framing: ICT Technicians shall use effective communication and interpersonal skills.
groups.explanation: This is the ability to work with others constructively, to explain ideas and proposals clearly and to discuss issues objectively and constructively.
groups.statementsIntro: The applicant shall demonstrate that they:

statements.text: Communicate technical and other information effectively in English1
illustrativeExamples: Contributing to meetings and discussions
Preparing communications, documents and reports on technical matters
Exchanging information and providing advice to technical and non-technical colleagues

Examples of different kinds of documents and/or presentations you have prepared or contributed to with an emphasis on those that include technical information about an ICT solution, system, process or hardware or software component
Give examples of where you have had to prepare documents or presentations for technical and non-technical audiences or recipients

statements.text: Work effectively with colleagues, clients, suppliers or the public
illustrativeExamples: Contributing constructively as part of a team
Successfully resolving issues in discussions with team members, suppliers, clients and/or others
Persuading others to accept suggestions or recommendations
Identifying, agreeing and working towards collective goals

statements.text: Be aware of the needs and concerns of others, demonstrate personal and social skills and awareness of diversity and inclusion issues.
illustrativeExamples: Knowing and managing own emotions, strengths and weaknesses
Being confident and flexible in dealing with new and changing interpersonal situations
Creating, maintaining and enhancing productive working relationships, and resolving conflicts
Being supportive of the needs and concerns of others, especially where this relates to diversity and inclusion

footnotes: 1 Any interviews will be conducted in English, subject only to the provisions of the Welsh Language Act 1993.

groups.title: Personal and professional commitment
groups.framing: ICT Technicians shall demonstrate commitment to an appropriate code of professional conduct, recognising obligations to society, the profession and the environment.
groups.explanation: This competence is about ensuring that the applicant is acting in a professional manner in their work and in their dealings with others. An ICT Technician should set a standard and example to others with regard to professionalism.
groups.statementsIntro: The applicant shall demonstrate that they:

statements.text: Understand and comply with relevant codes of conduct and regulations/standards
illustrativeExamples: Demonstrating compliance with your Licensee’s Code of Professional Conduct
Working within all relevant legislative and regulatory frameworks, including social and employment legislation

statements.text:
Manage and apply healthy, safe, secure systems of work, and be aware of appropriate hazard identification and risk management systems. This could include an ability to:
• Identify and take responsibility for own obligations for health, safety and welfare issues
• Apply systems that satisfy health, safety and welfare requirements
illustrativeExamples: Providing evidence of applying current safety requirements, such as risk assessment and other examples of good practice you adopt in your work
A sound knowledge of health and safety legislation, for example: HASAW 1974, CDM regulations, ISO 45001 and company safety policies
Recognising how sustainability principles, as described in the Guidance on Sustainability on page 26, can be applied in your day-to-day work
Identifying actions that you can and have taken to improve sustainability
Demonstrating awareness of environmental sustainability and the general recognition of sustainability

statements.text: Show you are aware of and apply good practices that protect other people, organisations or the environment from harm caused by the operation of ICT systems. Undertake ICT work in a way that contributes to sustainable development
illustrativeExamples: Understanding the ethical issues that you may encounter in your role
Giving an example of where you have applied ethical principles as described in the Statement of Ethical Principles on page 26
Giving an example of where you have applied or upheld ethical principles as defined by your organisation or company

statements.text:
Carry out and record CPD necessary to maintain and enhance competence in ICT including:
• Undertake reviews of own development needs
• Plan how to meet personal and organisational objectives
• Carry out planned and unplanned CPD activities
• Maintain evidence of competence development.
• Evaluate CPD outcomes against any plans made
• Assist others with their own CPD
illustrativeExamples: Undertaking reviews of your own development needs
Planning how to meet personal and organisational objectives
Carrying out and recording planned and unplanned CPD activities
Maintaining evidence of competence development
Evaluating CPD outcomes against any plans made
Assisting others with their own CPD
